records.title: ENIAC numerical weather prediction to operational JNWPU forecasting
records.sourceNativeSummary: By 1950 electronic calculation enabled a nonlinear numerical weather forecast that would have been operationally impossible by hand; by the mid-1950s a joint unit began routine numerical forecasting and repeatedly updated model/data procedures.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Faster computation did not make atmospheric prediction automatically accurate: initialization, observations, numerical balance, model physics and latency remained coupled constraints.

sources.supports: ENIAC-era numerical forecasting and operational progression
1950 nonlinear forecast, JNWPU and 1950s operational development

records.title: US Interstate Highway System as standardized transport infrastructure
records.sourceNativeSummary: The 1956 Federal-Aid Highway Act supplied the funding/governance mechanism for rapid Interstate construction with nationwide design expectations and a 90% federal cost share, converting decades of proposals into a national network buildout.
records.rivalOrBoundary: A connected high-capacity network produced mobility/economic value but also urban displacement, induced traffic and environmental effects; network completion is not a single-axis welfare metric.

sources.supports: 1956 Act as start of major Interstate construction
funding, nationwide standards, system integration and expansion

records.title: US Aircraft Nuclear Propulsion program: sustained research without deployable aircraft
records.sourceNativeSummary: U.S. programs built and tested reactor/engine subsystems for nuclear aircraft through the 1950s, but shielding, reactor/engine weight, safety and mission/system integration prevented a viable operational aircraft and the program was cancelled in the early 1960s.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Real subsystem tests and large expenditure did not prove whole-aircraft viability; the failure boundary is system mass/safety/mission closure rather than “no technical progress occurred.”

sources.supports: ANP goal, tests, engineering/safety problems and cancellation
nuclear aircraft engine programs and cancellation drivers

records.title: Project Mohole: ambitious deep-ocean drilling program cancelled before core objective
records.sourceNativeSummary: Project Mohole demonstrated dynamic-position/deep-water drilling feasibility in 1961 pilot holes but escalating management, technical and financial problems led Congress to terminate the program before drilling through ocean crust to the Moho.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Program failure did not imply zero scientific option value: methods/institutional lessons contributed to later deep-sea drilling, but later success cannot retroactively make Mohole’s original cost/management path successful.

sources.supports: NSF account of Mohole as management/financial failure and later deep-ocean legacy

records.title: Bristol Brabazon: technically ambitious postwar airliner without viable transport demand fit
records.sourceNativeSummary: Britain’s giant Brabazon prototype flew successfully in 1949 and demonstrated major airframe/infrastructure engineering, but the luxury low-density transatlantic demand model failed to attract customers; the project was cancelled in 1953 after one prototype.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Technical flight success and impressive subsystem engineering did not imply product-market/airline economics; infrastructure and experience retained option value for later Bristol programs.

sources.supports: design premise, flight success, lack of airline interest, costs and cancellation

records.title: Penzias-Wilson observation and Princeton relic-radiation prediction converging on the CMB
records.sourceNativeSummary: Penzias and Wilson encountered persistent unexplained microwave antenna noise while a Princeton group was preparing to search for relic Big-Bang radiation; contact between groups joined observation and interpretation in paired 1965 papers.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Observation and explanatory theory arose from partly independent lineages; the antenna result did not acquire cosmological meaning solely from its raw signal, and the prediction did not become empirical evidence until bound to observation.

sources.supports: independent Bell Labs observation and Princeton interpretation
Holmdel instrument/noise investigation and CMB identification

records.title: Baran and Davies independently developing packet-switching network concepts
records.sourceNativeSummary: Paul Baran in the U.S. and Donald Davies in Britain independently developed packetized/distributed networking concepts in the 1960s; ARPANET design later combined strands from multiple researchers and adopted the packet terminology.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Priority should not be collapsed into one inventor; the concepts did not themselves provide a deployed interoperable network, which required IMPs, lines, host software and protocols.

sources.supports: parallel Baran/Davies/Kleinrock packet-network work and later ARPANET convergence
independent Baran/Davies packet-switching concept and technical motivation
